definitions.explanation: The quality or degree of being short, whether in physical length, duration of time, or extent.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}の{日|ひ}の{短|みじか}さに{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was surprised by the shortness of winter days.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}の{短|みじか}さを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: I feel the brevity of life.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{短|みじか}さが{魅力|みりょく}で、{忙|いそが}しい{人|ひと}にもおすすめだ。
examples.english: The appeal of this movie is its brevity, so I recommend it even for busy people.

notes:
Formed by adding the suffix 〜さ to the adjective {短|みじか}い (short), converting it into a noun expressing the degree or quality of shortness. The 〜さ suffix is productive and can be applied to most i-adjectives (e.g., {長|なが}さ "length," {高|たか}さ "height").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人生|じんせい}の{短|みじか}さ: the brevity of life
- {日|ひ}の{短|みじか}さ: the shortness of days
- {時間|じかん}の{短|みじか}さ: the shortness of time
- {短|みじか}さが{魅力|みりょく}: brevity is its appeal

COMMON PATTERNS:
The 〜さ suffix turns i-adjectives into nouns expressing degree or extent. It attaches to the stem (without the final い): {短|みじか}い → {短|みじか}さ, {長|なが}い → {長|なが}さ, {高|たか}い → {高|たか}さ.
